field.label: Enable
field.help: Run the LunaShare rendezvous server. It only introduces devices to each other; chat and files go directly between the devices, end-to-end encrypted.

field.label: Port
field.help: Port the devices use to reach this server (default 47830): UDP - and also TCP when "Links for anyone" is on (the devices keep a TCP connection on it for the links). In LunaShare enter your public address or DynDNS name and this port, for example home.example.com:47830.

field.label: Listen address
field.help: Leave empty to listen on all IPv4 addresses.

field.label: Allow on WAN
field.help: Automatically add the firewall rules on the WAN interface: UDP to the port above, and with "Links for anyone" on also TCP to the port above and to the links' port. Disable this if you prefer to create the rules yourself (then remember the TCP ones for links).

field.label: Allowed rooms
field.help: Optional. Only devices using one of these rooms may register. Copy the room hash from LunaShare (Settings, Internet, "Copy room hash"). Leave empty to allow any room; room names and passwords still keep different groups apart.

field.label: Relay when direct fails
field.help: When two devices can't reach each other directly (for example both on mobile data behind carrier-grade NAT), pass their packets through this server. The data stays end-to-end encrypted; the server can't read it, but it does use your upload bandwidth.

field.label: Relay limit (kbit/s)
field.help: Bandwidth limit per relayed connection and direction. 0 = unlimited.

field.label: Keep messages for offline devices
field.help: Text messages for a device that is not reachable wait here until it comes online (end-to-end encrypted: the server can't read them or see who sent them). Stored in /var/db/lunashare.

field.label: Keep offline messages (days)
field.help: Messages nobody picked up are deleted after this many days.

field.label: Links for anyone
field.help: Lets people in your rooms send a file as a link that anyone can open in a web browser, without LunaShare (for example by SMS). The page is served here; the file comes from the sender's device through this server while they're online, end-to-end encrypted (the key is in the link after #, which browsers never send), and every part is checked in the browser. Nothing is stored here. Devices that joined with an invite can't make such links.

field.label: Links: HTTPS port
field.help: TCP port of the link pages (default 47831; it must not be the port of this web interface). Devices also connect to TCP on the UDP port above. With "Allow on WAN" both TCP ports are opened on WAN.

field.label: Links: certificate
field.help: A certificate for your public name (for example one from the ACME client plugin, Let's Encrypt). Browsers need HTTPS for these pages. After a renewal restart this service (the ACME plugin can do that with an automation), or it keeps the old one.

field.label: Links: public address
field.help: Only when a reverse proxy (HAProxy, nginx, Caddy) serves the pages with HTTPS: its address, for example https://share.example.com. This server then speaks plain HTTP on the port above (keep it closed on WAN) and takes the visitor's address from X-Forwarded-For.
